quick.summary: Why a huge change gets a quick looks fine, and how small ones get real review.
quick.takeaway: One purpose per change. Small enough to read properly.

beats.line: My change touched forty files. The review said looks fine. Then it broke production. How?
Nobody can really read forty files. So they skimmed.
But it was all one project.
One project, many changes. Split it by purpose.
The rename alone. Then the new logic. Then the cleanup.
Three reviews instead of one? That is slower.
Each takes minutes and gets read. One giant one waits days, unread.
First change: only the rename. No behaviour changes.
Now the reviewer can spot the one line that matters.

quiz.question: Why do small code changes get better reviews?
options: A reviewer can read all of it carefully
quiz.explanation: A change small enough to read fully gets real attention, so problems are caught.

quiz.question: Splitting a big change into several small ones usually makes review slower overall.
quiz.explanation: Small changes are read and approved quickly; one huge change waits and is skimmed.
